# 1 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_006_page_001.jpg

---

1. Now the king Antiochus was going through the upper provinces, and he heard that in Persia there was a city called Elymais, famous for its riches in silver and gold,
2. and that the temple in it was very wealthy, with golden shields and breastplates and weapons which Alexander son of Philip the Macedonian king, who reigned first among the Greeks, had left there.
3. And he came and sought to take the city and to plunder it; but he was not able, because the plan became known to the men of the city,
4. and they rose up against him in battle, and he fled and went away with great grief, to return to Babylon.
5. And a messenger came to him in Persia telling him that the armies that had gone into the land of Judah had been routed,
6. and that Lysias had gone with a strong force, and had been driven back before them, and that they had grown strong in arms and force and many plunders which they had taken from the armies which they had cut down,
7. and that they had pulled down the abomination which he had built upon the altar in Jerusalem, and that they had surrounded the sanctuary with high walls as before, and also Beth-zur, his city.
8. And it came to pass, when the king heard these words, he was astonished and greatly moved; and he lay down upon his bed and fell into sickness from grief, because it had not fallen out to him as he had intended.
9. And he was there many days, because great grief was renewed upon him, and he concluded that he was dying.
10. And he called all his Friends and said to them, "Sleep has departed from my eyes, and I am troubled in heart from care.
11. And I said in my heart, 'How great is the tribulation to which I have come, and into what a great flood I am now, — I, who was kindly and beloved in my power!'
12. And now I remember the evils I did in Jerusalem, and I took from there all the vessels of gold and silver; and I sent to destroy the inhabitants of Judah for no cause.
13. And I know that it is for this that these evils have found me; and behold, I am perishing with great grief in a strange land."
14. And he called Philip, one of his Friends, and set him over all his kingdom.
15. And he gave him his diadem and his robe and his signet ring, to lead Antiochus his son and bring him up to be king.
16. And King Antiochus died there in the one hundred and forty-ninth year.
17. And Lysias learned that the king was dead, and he set up his son Antiochus to reign, whom he had brought up as a young child; and he called his name Eupator.
18. Now those who were in the citadel were besieging Israel round about the sanctuary, and they were continually seeking their hurt and strengthening the nations.
19. And Judas thought to destroy them, and he gathered all the people together to besiege them.
20. And they gathered together and besieged them in the one hundred and fiftieth year; and he built machines and engines of war against them.
21. And some of those besieged went out, and certain ungodly men of Israel joined them,
22. and they went to the king and said, "How long will you not do judgment and avenge our brothers?
23. We were willing to serve your father, and to walk according to his words, and to follow his orders.
24. And our own people have been besieging us on account of this, and whoever of us they could seize they killed, and they plundered our inheritances.
25. And it is not against us alone that they stretched out their hand, but against all their borders.
26. And behold, they encamp today against the citadel in Jerusalem to take it; and they have fortified the sanctuary and Beth-zur.
27. And if you do not go ahead of them quickly, they will do greater things than these, and you will not be able to control them."
28. And the king was wroth when he heard this; and he gathered all his Friends and the commanders of his forces and those over the cavalry.
29. And hired forces came to him from other kingdoms and from the islands of the sea.
30. And the number of his forces was a hundred thousand foot soldiers and twenty thousand horsemen and thirty-two elephants trained for war.
31. And they went through Idumea and encamped before Beth-zur; and they fought against it many days and made engines of war; and the besieged sallied out and burned them with fire, and fought bravely.
32. And Judas departed from the citadel and encamped at Beth-zechariah, over against the camp of the king.
33. And the king rose early in the morning and moved his forces in haste along the road to Beth-zechariah; and the armies made ready for battle and sounded the trumpets.
34. And they showed the elephants the juice of grapes and mulberries, to prepare them for battle.
35. And they distributed the beasts among the phalanxes; and with each elephant they stationed a thousand men armed with coats of mail and with bronze helmets on their heads; and five hundred horsemen chosen were assigned to each beast.
36. These were ready beforehand wherever the beast was; and wherever it went they went with it, and they did not separate from it.
37. And upon the elephants were wooden towers, strong and covered, fastened upon each of them with special harness; and upon each were four armed men who fought from there, and also an Indian driver.
38. And the remaining horsemen were placed on this side and on that side, at the two flanks of the army, to harass the enemy and to be protected in the midst of the companies.
39. And when the sun shone upon the golden shields and the bronze shields, the mountains gleamed with them and blazed like torches of fire.
40. And part of the king's army spread out upon the high mountains, and some on the lower ground, and they marched confidently and in order.
41. And all the inhabitants of the land were astonished at the sound of their multitude, and the marching of the companies, and the clashing of the weapons; for the army was very great and mighty.
42. And Judas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men from the king's army fell.
43. And Eleazar who was called Avaran saw that one of the beasts was armed with royal armor, and it was higher than all the beasts; and he supposed that the king was on it,
44. and he gave his life to save his people and to get himself an everlasting name.
45. And he ran upon it boldly into the midst of the phalanx, and slew on the right hand and on the left, and they parted asunder before him on this side and on that.
46. And he crept under the elephant, and thrust under it and slew it; and the elephant fell to the earth upon him, and he died there.
47. But when the Judeans saw the strength of the kingdom and the fierce onset of the forces, they turned away from them.
48. And the forces of the king went up against them to Jerusalem, and the forces of the king encamped against Judea and against Mount Zion.
49. And he made peace with the men of Beth-zur; and they came out of the city, because they had no food there to endure the siege, for it was a sabbatical year for the land.
50. And the king took Beth-zur and stationed a garrison there to hold it.
51. And he encamped against the sanctuary many days; and he set up there machines of war and engines, and instruments of fire and throwing stones, and pieces to cast arrows, and slings.
52. And they also made war machines against their machines, and they held out for many days.
53. But there were no provisions in the storerooms, because it was the seventh year, and those who had taken refuge in Judea from the nations had eaten up the remnant of the provisions.
54. And only a few were left in the sanctuary, because hunger had prevailed over them, and they were scattered each to his own place.
55. And Lysias heard that Philip, whom Antiochus the king while he still lived had appointed to bring up his son Antiochus to be king,
56. had returned from Persia and Media and with him the forces that went with the king, and that he was seeking to take over the government.
57. And he was in haste to go and said to the king and the commanders of the forces and the men, "We decay day by day, and our provision is scant, and the place against which we are fighting is strong; and the affairs of the kingdom need us.
58. Now therefore let us give the right hand to these men and make peace with them and with all their nation,
59. and covenant with them that they shall walk according to their customs as before; for on account of their customs which we abolished, they were angered and did all these things."
60. And the word was good in the eyes of the king and the commanders; and he sent to them to make peace, and they received it.
61. And the king and the commanders swore to them upon all these conditions; and they came out of the stronghold.
62. And the king entered Mount Zion; and he saw the strength of the place, and he broke the oath which he had sworn, and commanded to pull down the wall round about.
63. And he departed in haste and returned to Antioch, and he found Philip holding the city; and he fought against him and took the city by force.
